name: Linen
weight: Light to heavy, about 110 to 250 gsm
swatch: repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(150,120,80,.18) 0 1px, transparent 1px 4px), repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255,255,255,.35) 0 1px, transparent 1px 5px), #D9CBB2
feel: Cool, crisp at first and softer with every wash. Wrinkles in a relaxed, lived-in way.
tips: Pre-wash: linen can shrink noticeably.
Finish every seam, it frays.
Press with steam while slightly damp.
care: Machine wash gentle, line dry, iron damp.

name: Cotton poplin
weight: Light to medium, about 100 to 140 gsm
feel: Smooth, crisp and stable. Holds a press beautifully and is easy to sew.
tips: A great fabric for beginners: it doesn't slip or stretch.
Pre-wash to avoid shrinking later.
care: Machine wash warm, tumble or line dry.

name: Cotton voile & lawn
feel: Light, soft and a little see-through. Lawn is slightly smoother and denser than voile.
tips: French seams look lovely and hide raw edges.
Hold it up to the light: some colours need a lining.

name: Double gauze
weight: Light to medium, about 120 to 160 gsm
feel: Two soft layers of gauze tacked together. Airy, crinkly and very comfortable.
tips: Finish seams well, the layers can fray.
No need to press it flat, the crinkle is the charm.

name: Rayon (viscose) challis
weight: Light to medium, about 110 to 150 gsm
swatch: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, #8A2822 0 3px, transparent 4px) 0 0/22px 22px, radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, #F5D76E 0 2px, transparent 3px) 11px 11px/22px 22px, #F0DCD2
feel: Fluid, silky drape that swishes as you walk. Often printed with florals.
tips: Cut in a single layer, it shifts.
Use pattern weights instead of lots of pins.
Pre-wash: it can shrink.
care: Hand or gentle wash cold, line dry.

name: Crepe
weight: Light to medium, about 100 to 200 gsm
feel: Slightly pebbly surface with a soft, heavy drape. Comes in polyester, viscose and silk.
tips: Press with a cloth and medium heat.
Some crepes have a little stretch, so stay-stitch curves.
care: Check the label; many are hand wash.

name: Satin
weight: Light to medium, about 80 to 160 gsm
feel: Glossy on one side, smooth and slippery. Catches the light beautifully.
tips: Pin only inside the seam allowance, pins leave marks.
Use a fresh sharp needle.
Press on the wrong side with a press cloth.
care: Usually hand wash cold or dry clean.

name: Chiffon & georgette
feel: Sheer and floaty. Georgette has a slightly grainier, less slippery feel.
tips: Lay tissue paper under it when cutting and sewing.
French seams and narrow rolled hems look best.

name: Gingham
weight: Light to medium, about 100 to 150 gsm
feel: A crisp woven check, usually cotton. Instantly cheerful and a little bit cottagecore.
tips: Buy extra to match checks at seams.
Cut in a single layer so the checks line up.
care: Machine wash, line or tumble dry.

name: Denim
weight: Medium to heavy, about 8 to 14 oz (270 to 475 gsm)
feel: Sturdy cotton twill with a diagonal weave. Stretch denim has a little elastane for comfort.
tips: Pre-wash: it shrinks and the dye can run.
Use a longer stitch and topstitch thread for the classic look.

name: Cotton twill & chino
weight: Medium to heavy, about 200 to 300 gsm
feel: Firm and durable with a fine diagonal rib. Holds sharp creases.
tips: Press seams open firmly, then topstitch if you like.
care: Machine wash, tumble or line dry.

name: Tencel (lyocell)
weight: Light to medium, about 120 to 200 gsm
feel: Smooth, cool and drapey with a soft sheen. Often called peach-skin when sanded.
tips: Shows needle holes, so unpick carefully.
Press at medium heat.

name: Cotton jersey
weight: Light to medium, about 150 to 220 gsm
feel: Soft T-shirt knit. Cotton spandex jersey has more stretch and recovery.
tips: Use a stretch stitch or narrow zigzag.
A walking foot stops wavy seams.
It won't fray, so hems are quick.
care: Machine wash cold, dry flat or tumble low.

name: Rib knit
weight: Light to medium, about 180 to 260 gsm
feel: Raised vertical ribs with lots of crosswise stretch and good snap-back.
tips: Cut bands slightly shorter than the opening and stretch as you sew.

name: French terry & sweatshirt fleece
weight: Medium to heavy, about 240 to 350 gsm
feel: Smooth on the outside with soft loops (terry) or brushed fluff (fleece) on the inside.
tips: Use a slightly longer stretch stitch.
Pair with rib knit for cuffs and waistbands.

name: Ponte
weight: Medium to heavy, about 250 to 350 gsm
feel: A stable double knit with gentle stretch. Smooth, thick and very forgiving.
tips: Easy for knit beginners: it doesn't curl at the edges.
A narrow zigzag is enough.
